questions.stem: What determines which element an atom belongs to?

options.text: The number of neutrons in the nucleus
The number of electrons in the shells
The number of protons in the nucleus
The total mass of the atom

questions.explanation: The number of protons in the nucleus uniquely defines which element an atom is. For example, all atoms with 6 protons are carbon, regardless of how many neutrons or electrons they have. While neutral atoms have equal protons and electrons, it is specifically the proton number that defines the element.

questions.stem: A student writes the symbol for cobalt as 'CO'. Why is this incorrect?

options.text: Cobalt should be written as 'Cb'
'CO' represents carbon monoxide (a compound), not cobalt; cobalt is 'Co'
Element symbols must always be a single letter
'CO' is the correct symbol for cobalt

questions.explanation: In chemical symbols, the first letter is always capitalised and the second letter (if present) is always lowercase. 'Co' represents the element cobalt, while 'CO' represents carbon monoxide - a compound made of carbon (C) and oxygen (O). This distinction is critical in chemistry.

questions.stem: The chemical symbol for potassium is K, derived from the Latin word 'Kalium'. Which other element also has a symbol derived from Latin?

options.text: Calcium (Ca)
Copper (Cu)
Carbon (C)
Chlorine (Cl)

questions.explanation: Copper has the symbol Cu, derived from the Latin word 'Cuprum'. Similarly, sodium is Na (Natrium), iron is Fe (Ferrum), gold is Au (Aurum), and lead is Pb (Plumbum). Calcium, carbon, and chlorine all have symbols directly from their English names.

questions.stem: Where is almost all the mass of an atom concentrated?

options.text: In the electron shells
Spread evenly throughout the atom
In the space between the nucleus and electron shells
In the nucleus

questions.explanation: Almost all the mass of an atom is concentrated in the nucleus, which contains protons and neutrons. Despite being very small compared to the overall atom (about 1/10,000 of the diameter), the nucleus contains nearly all the mass because electrons have negligible mass (about 1/1836 of a proton).

questions.stem: A pure substance contains only atoms with 8 protons. Another pure substance also contains only atoms with 8 protons. A student claims these must be different elements. Is the student correct?

options.text: Yes, because different samples always contain different elements
No, because both substances contain oxygen atoms since all atoms with 8 protons are oxygen
Yes, because the atoms could have different numbers of electrons
It depends on the number of neutrons in each atom

questions.explanation: Since both substances contain atoms with 8 protons, they are both oxygen. The number of protons defines the element, so any atom with 8 protons is oxygen regardless of the number of neutrons or electrons. The student is incorrect.
